title: Acting
summary: The agent changes the app when the user asks, through actions the product defines.
description: An action is a change the product lets the agent make, such as adding an entry or opening a screen. Adding and editing happen at once and can be undone; what would lose data waits for the user to confirm it.

requirements.text: The agent changes the app only through actions the product defines, never by writing SQL.
An action makes its change the way the app's own screens make it, with the same checks, and the change shows at once wherever that data shows.
There is an action for each change a user can make from the app's screens.
The agent makes a change only when the user asked for it; a change it thinks of itself, it proposes and waits.
An action that adds or edits happens at once, and shows in the chat as what changed, with a way to open it in the app and an undo.
An action that deletes or overwrites data is first proposed in the chat, saying what would be lost, and happens only once the user confirms it there; when the user declines, the agent is told.
Undo puts the data back as it was before the change, unless it has changed since, and then says so and changes nothing.
An action makes all of its change or none of it, and one that fails tells the agent why.
The agent can open a screen or an item in the app for the user.
